title: NHAI Unveils Uniform Design Verification Framework For Major Bridges And Critical Highway Structures
text:
Infrastructure
Swarajya Staff
Oct 16, 2026 | Updated 09:32 AM GMT+5:30
Save & read from anywhere!

The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) has introduced a uniform system for independent verification of designs and drawings for major bridges and critical structures across national highway projects.
The policy will come into effect on 1 December 2026, and apply to all new Engineering, Procurement and Construction (EPC), Hybrid Annuity Model (HAM) and Build-Operate-Transfer (BOT) National Highway projects.
It will also cover eligible ongoing projects in which design verification or proof-checking has not yet begun.
Under the new mechanism, designs will be examined independently by empanelled Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs), reputed government technical institutions and experienced technical firms.
Around 12 IITs, including IIT Delhi, IIT Bombay, IIT Roorkee and IIT Kharagpur, along with other premier institutions, have expressed willingness to participate in the initiative.
The move aims to strengthen structural safety and improve construction quality across India's highway network.
The verification will cover structural design calculations, engineering analysis and drawings, as well as hydrological and hydraulic studies wherever applicable.
The exercise is intended to identify potential design deficiencies at an early stage and ensure compliance with applicable Indian Roads Congress (IRC) codes, technical specifications and contractual requirements.
The policy covers major river bridges with a design discharge of at least 3,000 cubic metres per second, structures with an individual effective span of 40 metres or more, and other special or complex structures identified by NHAI.
Under the revised procedure, the contractor or concessionaire will submit the design and drawings for review or approval, as applicable under the contract. Three institutions or firms will then be proposed from NHAI's empanelled list.
Following independent verification, necessary modifications to designs will be considered before their review or approval by NHAI, in accordance with the applicable contractual provisions.
The initiative aims to detect design-related issues early and ensure major bridges, designed for a service life of 100 years or more, meet safety standards.
The framework will establish uniform quality assurance practices across different project delivery formats, creating a nationwide institutional mechanism for design vetting of critical bridge infrastructure.
Delays in completing the checks will not automatically entitle contractors to extensions or additional claims against NHAI.
